title: CDC looking into several items potentially linked to cyclospora parasite
summary: As of Tuesday, nearly 7,000 people in 34 states reported symptoms tied to a parasitic illness that, so far, has no official source. Carter Evans reports on what's suspected of being behind the cyclosporiasis outbreak.

title: Fire departments work to get rid of cancer-linked foam extinguisher: "It was like sitting on a bomb"
summary: Fire departments across the U.S. are changing how they extinguish fires. For decades, they used foam that contained so-called "forever chemicals" that are now linked to cancer. More than a dozen states are now working to collect, remove and destroy all of it. Mark Strassmann has more.

title: Michigan's cyclosporiasis outbreak grows to more than 1,500 cases
summary: Michigan health officials say the state's cyclosporiasis outbreak has grown to more than 1,500 cases.

title: What parents should know about the infant botulism outbreak caused by baby formula
summary: A fourth infant was hospitalized for botulism linked to Nara Organics baby formula, and the FDA is now expanding its investigation. Dr. Céline Gounder has the latest.

title: Medicare will now help pay for some GLP-1 drugs. Here's what to know
summary: Starting Wednesday, Medicare will help pay for some GLP-1 medications for weight loss. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Celine Gounder explains what this means for patients.

title: Behind the growing and controversial trend of looksmaxxing
summary: Looksmaxxing is a viral and controversial trend that encourages young men to maximize their appearance. Adam Yamaguchi shows why it's resonating with some people.

title: Former NFL star Chris Johnson says he's been diagnosed with ALS
summary: Former NFL running back Chris Johnson announced that he was diagnosed with ALS, also known as Lou Gehrig's disease, in a "Good Morning America" interview.

title: 6/21: Sunday Morning
summary: Hosted by Lee Cowan. Featured: Birthright citizenship; the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library unveiled; Shooter Jennings releases recordings by his father, Waylon Jennings; comedian John Mulaney; childhood obesity; and the secrets of seahorses and seadragons.

title: Fighting childhood obesity, for a healthier, longer life
summary: In 1970, about 1 in 20 children were affected by obesity; today, it's 1 in 5. Dr. Jonathan LaPook looks at programs aimed at helping kids (and their families) get healthy the old-fashioned way, by eating right and exercising.

title: Fighting childhood obesity, for a healthier, longer life
summary: In 1970, about 1 in 20 children were affected by obesity; today, it's 1 in 5, with diet and exercise both key factors in the increase. CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jonathan LaPook looks at programs aimed at helping kids get healthy the old-fashioned way, by eating right and exercising, while helping decrease the risk of problems tied to obesity…

title: Doctor goes above and beyond for her cancer patient, ending with a big surprise
summary: Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" with a story of a teen battling for his life and the doctor who made him a promise.

title: Busy Philipps opens up about receiving ADHD diagnosis later in life
summary: Actress Busy Philipps, 45, spoke up about her late attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder diagnosis online after realizing she shared symptoms as her young daughter was evaluated and diagnosed. Women are more likely than men to be diagnosed with ADHD later in life, research shows.

title: Drummer rediscovers passion for music after life-changing accident
summary: In the "CBS Mornings" series "Pushing the Limits," Mark Strassmann shows how a Georgia man's passion for music was almost taken away from him forever after a terrible accident. But thanks to his resilience and technology, the man is now a record-breaking drummer.

title: FDA approves new sunscreen ingredient
summary: The FDA approved a new ingredient for sunscreen that's been in use in Europe for years. Dr. Jon LaPook has more details.

title: Safety concerns over doctors prescribing experimental weight loss drug not approved by FDA
summary: There's a new safety concern about doctors prescribing one experimental weight loss treatment, retatrutide, that hasn't even been FDA approved yet. Adam Yamaguchi reports.

title: The promises and pitfalls of GLP-1 drugs
summary: Approved 20 years ago as a diabetes treatment, GLP-1 drugs have been found to help patients reduce weight, changing the lives of more than 30 million people in the U.S. But there also have been troubling side effects reported.

title: The promises and pitfalls of GLP-1 drugs
summary: Approved 20 years ago as a treatment for diabetes, GLP-1 drugs have been found also to help patients significantly reduce weight. More than 30 million people in the U.S. have had their lives changed by GLP-1 medications. But there have also been troubling side effects reported. Correspondent Tracy Smith talks with experts who say the drugs might prove usefu…

title: Insulin inhaler could become alternative for Type 1 diabetes insulin injections
summary: A medical breakthrough is showing promise for millions of Americans with Type 1 diabetes. It's an alternative to taking insulin without the injections. Mark Strassmann has more details.

title: FDA launches safety study for abortion pill mifepristone, source says
summary: The Food and Drug Administration has launched a safety study of the abortion pill mifepristone, a senior FDA official confirmed to CBS News, a step that could pave the way for the Trump administration to restrict access to the medication.

title: What makes promising pancreatic cancer drug different from chemotherapy?
summary: A new drug was shown in trials to keep pancreatic cancer patients alive for twice as long as chemotherapy alone. Dr. Jon LaPook has more.

title: Americans on health insurance: "I pay a lot of money for and it covers very little"
summary: In the 1800s, Hartford, Connecticut, picked up the nickname, "The Insurance Capital of the World." Tony Dokoupil visits the city to ask people about rising insurance and healthcare costs.

title: HGTV host Ty Pennington opens up about his mom's battle with a chronic lung condition
summary: HGTV host and designer Ty Pennington opens up about his mother's yearslong battle with bronchiectasis, a chronic lung condition that often goes undiagnosed, and shares tips for caregivers on creating a calm environment. (Sponsored by Insmed)

title: Trump has third medical exam of the past year
summary: President Trump said his health "checked out perfectly" after a medical checkup on Tuesday. Nancy Cordes reports.

title: New weight-loss drug Retatrutide showing stronger results than current options
summary: A new weight-loss drug, so new it is not on the market yet, is showing promising results in trials, doing much more than what current medications can. Dr. Jon LaPook breaks it down.

title: Is "fibermaxxing" good for your health?
summary: Health and fitness influencers are pushing people to consume more fiber. Keri Glassman, Nutritious Life founder and CEO, joins with her take.

title: Vanessa Trump announces breast cancer diagnosis
summary: Vanessa Trump announced on Instagram that she has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is working with her doctors on a treatment plan.

title: Noah Wyle on his push to help healthcare workers
summary: Noah Wyle, who stars in HBO's "The Pitt," joins "CBS Mornings" with Dr. Elisabeth Potter to discuss their push to improve mental health and quality of life for healthcare workers.

title: Controversial FDA official leaving drug center post in latest departure at agency
summary: Dr. Tracy Beth Høeg, leader of the Food and Drug Administration division responsible for regulating prescription and over-the-counter drugs, is leaving her post, a senior FDA official confirmed.

title: How teenagers, McDonalds and a cellphone added up to a life-changing moment
summary: Three South Florida teenagers helped a 65-year-old having a heart attack. Matt Gutman has the story.

title: Jake Rosmarin, passenger from hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, on quarantine experience
summary: Jake Rosmarin, a travel influencer who was on the M/V Hondius as it suffered a hantavirus outbreak, is one of 16 Americans quarantining at the University of Nebraska Medical Center. Rosmarin spoke with CBS News about how a five-week trip is now stretching into 12 weeks away from home.

title: American monitored for hantavirus: "I'm just ready to cope" with quarantine
summary: Jake Rosmarin is one of the 16 Americans at the University of Nebraska Medical Center being monitored for signs of hantavirus. Ian Lee spoke with him and has more details.

title: New Yorker describes hantavirus quarantine experience after cruise ship outbreak
summary: A New York native is among 16 American passengers who are quarantining in Nebraska after being on the cruise ship that is at the center of the deadly hantavirus outbreak.

title: How physical activity can boost your brain health and reduce dementia risk
summary: Daily physical activity is one of the important steps to building healthy habits to lower the risk of dementia. As part of a three-part series, "Brain Health: From Awareness to Action," Alzheimer's Association President and CEO Joanne Pike joins "CBS Mornings" with tips on incorporating exercise into your routine as part of their "(re)think your brain" init…

title: Americans enter quarantine after returning from hantavirus cruise ship
summary: The 18 Americans who were aboard a hantavirus-stricken cruise ship have returned to the U.S. and are now in quarantine. One remains in the biocontainment unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center after testing positive. Ian Lee has more.

title: NIH director on hantavirus risk
summary: Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, director of the National Institutes of Health and acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, spoke with "CBS Evening News" anchor Tony Dokoupil about what risks hantavirus poses to the U.S. public.

title: Man who survived hantavirus 24 years ago, but lost mom and sister, recounts experience
summary: In 2002, Zermeño found out he contracted hantavirus after cleaning the family house following the death of his mother and sister. He had been exposed to rodent droppings and became infected.

title: Health officials track passengers tied to hantavirus-stricken cruise ship
summary: Global health officials are working to track down passengers who departed a hantavirus-stricken cruise ship weeks ago, including multiple Americans. Meanwhile, for the first time on Thursday, President Trump addressed the response to the deadly outbreak. Tom Hanson has the latest on the cruise ship and Dr. Celine Gounder breaks down what to know about the v…

title: What's the hantavirus risk to the public?
summary: A deadly strain of hantavirus broke out aboard a cruise ship for the first time, with more than 150 people on board. With three deaths among eight confirmed cases so far, Dr. Céline Gounder discusses the wider risks.

title: A tool to help keep dementia in check
summary: Many people fear that a family history of dementia dooms them to inevitably suffer the condition themselves. But a new tool, the Brain Care Score, shows how lifestyle changes can be beneficial, cutting the risk of dementia.

title: A tool to help keep dementia in check
summary: Many people fear that a family history of dementia dooms them to inevitably suffer the condition themselves. But a new tool, the Brain Care Score, shows how lifestyle changes can be beneficial, cutting the risk of dementia. National Public Radio correspondent Allison Aubrey talks with neurologist Dr. Jonathan Rosand about how making changes to your daily ha…

title: Horsepower: How horses are therapeutic
summary: Horses can form powerful bonds with people owing to their ability to sense and feel human emotions. Endeavor Therapeutic Horsemanship, in Bedford Corners, N.Y., has programs that help people with disabilities, veterans with PTSD, and the incarcerated through interactions with their horses. "60 Minutes" correspondent Lesley Stahl reports.

title: Trump nominates Dr. Erica Schwartz for new CDC director
summary: President Trump nominated a new director for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Thursday. Dr. Erica Schwartz is a former deputy surgeon general and retired Coast Guard rear admiral.

title: Trump to sign executive order on psychedelic drug used abroad to treat PTSD
summary: Ibogaine is used in Mexico and the Caribbean to treat depression, anxiety, addiction and brain trauma.
